{{Short description|German biophysicist (born 1943)}}
'''Roland Benz''' (born 1943 in [[Singen]], [[Baden-Württemberg]]; died 2025 in [[Würzburg]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/constructor-university_constructor-university-mourns-the-loss-of-activity-7297168133973315584-Fkfh |title=Constructor University mourns the loss of Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. multi. Roland Benz |website=linkedin.com |date=March 2025 |access-date=2025-09-06}}</ref>) was a German [[biophysicist]].

==Early life and education==
Benz studied [[mathematics]], [[chemistry]], and [[physics]] at the [[University of Würzburg]]. In 1972, he obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy#Germany|Ph.D.]] in biology, with [[Peter Läuger]] at [[University of Konstanz]] as his supervisor; and, in 1977, he obtained his [[Habilitation]] in [[Biophysics]].

==Career==
A Heisenberg Fellow of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG)]] (German Science Foundation), Benz was a [[visiting scholar|visiting professor]] at [[Stony Brook University|State University of New York at Stony Brook]] (SUNYSB) in 1980 and 1982. In 1984, he was a visiting professor at [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Vancouver]].

In 1986, Benz became a full professor of [[biotechnology]] at the University of Würzburg, his ''alma mater''.

Since 2003, Benz has been a Member of the European Graduate College;{{citation needed|date=July 2012}} and, since 2005, a Member in the French–German Graduate College, both sponsored by the DFG.{{citation needed|date=July 2012}}

Since 2009, Benz held the Wisdom Professorship at the [[Jacobs University Bremen]]<ref>[http://www.jacobs-university.de/news/rolandbenz "Swedish honors for Jacobs Wisdom Professor Roland Benz"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104133349/http://www.jacobs-university.de/news/rolandbenz |date=2013-11-04 }}, Jacobs University Bremen, 10 June 2011</ref> and has been a research fellow at the [[Rudolf Virchow Center]] and the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG Research Center]] for Experimental Biomedicine.

===Research interests===
Benz's research interests included the periplasmic structure and organization of [[cell membrane]]s and other [[biological membrane]]s; biophysical processes and the molecular basis of membrane [[protein]]s in [[microorganism]]s and higher organisms; and, pore-forming [[peptide]]s and proteins.

Benz was the leader of several research projects, including:
*the molecular basis of signal transduction and membrane transport (SFB 176; 1987–1999);
*ecology, physiology, and biochemistry of plants under stress (SFB 251; 1989–1992);
*nuclear magnetic resonance ''in vivo'' and in vitro for the study of biomedical basic elements (Member in the DFG-Graduate College; 1992–1999); and,
*the regulatory membrane proteins: from the mechanism of recognition to the pharmacological structure (SFB 487; seit 2000).

===Awards===
In 2002, Benz was recognised with the ''Gay-Lussac/Humboldt Award de la Ministère de recherche français'' for his role in the development of a Franco–German collaboration.{{citation needed|date=July 2012}}

In 2007, he was awarded an honorary doctorate by the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref>[http://www.ub.edu/gpre/Benz.pdf "Solemne Investiturade Doctor honoris causa Roland Benz"], Universitat de Barcelona, November 2007</ref>

In 2011, he was honoured, with another honorary doctorate, by the [[Umeå University]]'s Faculty of Medicine<ref>[http://www.mims.umu.se/en/news-events/1396-roland-benz-honorary-doctor-at-umea-university.html "Roland Benz honorary doctor at Umeå University"], Laboratory for Molecular Infection Medicine Sweden (MIMS), Juni 2011</ref>

===Publications===
* Benz R. (1980.) ''Künstliche Lipidmembranen. Modelle für biologische Membranen'', Universitätsverlag Konstanz, {{ISBN|3-87940-142-X}}
* Benz R. (2004.) ''Bacterial and Eukaryotic Porins. Structure, Function, Mechanism'', Wiley-VCH, {{ISBN|3-527-30775-3}}
